summary: First full-pass testing of 'What Can I Eat?' app. Backend (6/6 pytest) and frontend (all E2E flows) PASSED. /api/scan correctly identifies ingredients from a real fridge JPEG using GPT-4o vision; /api/suggest returns 3-5 well-structured recipes; validation 400s on empty inputs. Frontend: Home hero buttons navigate correctly to /scan and /scan?mode=manual, manual ingredient entry (Enter + add button + chip remove + clear all) works, find-recipes call hits /api/suggest and lands on /results with 3-5 recipe cards, recipe detail page shows instructions/ingredients/missing, 'Add missing to shopping list' populates the Shopping page with toggleable (line-through) and removable items, Clear list works, mobile shopping-badge shows correct unchecked count, desktop top-nav and mobile bottom-nav both navigate correctly.

issues: Emergent system 'Made with Emergent' badge slightly overlaps the bottom nav on small viewports (390x844). This is the platform overlay, not an app bug — flagging for awareness only.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses deprecated FastAPI '@app.on_event("shutdown")' — consider migrating to lifespan handlers (non-blocking).

scan endpoint validates only by len(b64) < 100; it does not verify the base64 actually decodes to a JPEG/PNG/WEBP. A malformed but >=100-char string would be passed to the LLM. Consider verifying magic bytes (FFD8FF / 89504E47 / RIFF) before sending to the model.

Difficulty Pydantic field is free-form str; LLM is instructed only 'easy' or 'medium' but 'hard' would also pass since model has no Literal/Enum constraint. Consider using Literal['easy','medium','hard'].
Frontend stores recipes in localStorage which can grow large; no size guard. Low priority.

Frontend Scan.jsx merges newly scanned ingredients with existing (good), but there is no per-name normalization beyond lowercase trim — duplicates like 'tomato' vs 'tomatoes' may both persist. Acceptable for MVP.
seed_data_creation: Downloaded a real Pexels fridge JPEG to /tmp/fridge.jpg (used by test_scan_real_image_returns_ingredients).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests at /app/backend/tests/test_api.py expect /tmp/fridge.jpg to exist (a real JPEG of a fridge/groceries). If missing, re-download with: curl -s -o /tmp/fridge.jpg 'https://images.pexels.com/photos/31485991/pexels-photo-31485991.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=800'. The app uses localStorage so Playwright sessions start with empty state — to test /results/recipe/shopping flow, complete the manual-ingredients -> find-recipes flow inside the same Playwright session. AI calls (scan ~3-10s, suggest ~5-30s) need generous timeouts (120s suggested).
